title: NEB Class 12 Mathematics — Integration — 2024
subject: mathematics
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Evaluate: (a) ∫ x eˣ dx, (b) ∫ dx/(x² − 4).
questions.solution:
**(a) By parts** (∫u dv = uv − ∫v du): take u = x, dv = eˣdx → du = dx, v = eˣ.

∫x eˣ dx = x eˣ − ∫eˣ dx = **x eˣ − eˣ + C = eˣ(x − 1) + C**.

**(b) Partial fractions:** 1/(x² − 4) = 1/[(x − 2)(x + 2)] = (1/4)[1/(x − 2) − 1/(x + 2)].

So ∫dx/(x² − 4) = **(1/4) ln|(x − 2)/(x + 2)| + C** (using ∫dx/(x − a) = ln|x − a|).
questions.knowledgeNote: For by-parts choose u by the ILATE order (Inverse, Log, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential) — here the algebraic x is u.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫₀^(π/2) sin²x dx.
questions.solution:
Use the identity sin²x = (1 − cos2x)/2:

∫sin²x dx = ∫(1 − cos2x)/2 dx = x/2 − sin2x/4.

Applying the limits 0 to π/2: [π/4 − 0] − [0 − 0] = **π/4 ≈ 0.785**.

(Check by symmetry: ∫₀^(π/2) sin²x dx = ∫₀^(π/2) cos²x dx, and their sum is π/2, so each is π/4.)
questions.knowledgeNote: Reducing powers with double-angle identities converts a definite trigonometric integral into elementary terms — the standard NEB approach.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫ dx/(1 + cos x).
questions.solution:
Use 1 + cos x = 2cos²(x/2):

∫ dx/(1 + cosx) = ∫ dx/(2cos²(x/2)) = (1/2)∫ sec²(x/2) dx = (1/2)·2 tan(x/2) + C = **tan(x/2) + C**.

So the integral is tan(x/2) + C (valid where cos(x/2) ≠ 0).
questions.knowledgeNote: Half-angle identities turn rational trigonometric integrands into standard sec² forms — remember ∫sec²u du = tan u.
